_doc: The DURABLE source of record for tracking_issue (caps.db is gitignored). reconcile-tracking-issues.mjs upserts these into caps.db on every rebuild; track.mjs (pnpm caps:track) edits this file + the DB together. Seeded 2026-06-19 from the previously-scattered findings (the DB-truth audit, the F1-F4 money audit, the truth-gate cleanup, production-readiness escalations, and open product/doc gaps). severity P0..P4; status open|in_progress|fixed|wontfix|deferred; autonomous_safe 1 = fixable without a human decision.

issues.title: Money-action pre-approval replay / confused deputy
issues.detail: money_action_pre_approved did not bind the approval to amount/operation/provider/reversibility and was not single-use; a non-board agent could replay any approved row to commit a $1M irreversible payout.

issues.detail: commerce.rs mints CostRecord+BrowserFinanceRecord on an armed click with no dollar-band / budget hard-stop; exposes to_side_effect_action() but never calls it. NOT exploitable today: zero crates depend on chronica-internet-hand (un-wired). HARD RULE: do NOT wire until its money path routes through evaluate_gate -> commit_money_action.

issues.title: Inventory found-stock valued at $0 auto-allows past gate
issues.detail: DEBT.BATCH-1 (2026-09) re-audit: the historical adjustment_action positive-units_delta path (crates/chronica-erp/src/inventory/mod.rs, the old flat crate) does not exist anywhere in the current codebase -- extinguished by refoundation, not superseded by a targeted patch. Current source-to-sink for positive stock: POST /api/companies/:company_id/inventory/ledger/receive (chronica-cap-erp-commerce-ops-routes/src/inventory.rs::receive_stock) requires an explicit body `unitCostCents` field (422 UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY if absent or negative) for every receipt, into an empty ledger or not; chronica_cap_inventory_ledger::record_receipt always forwards that caller-supplied value straight to StockLedger::receive, with no default/derived-zero fallback. avco_unit_cost_cents()==0 only ever occurs on a truly empty ledger (0 on-hand units) and is read only inside StockLedger::issue's own COGS calculation (issue() itself refuses when units>on_hand, so it can never run against an empty ledger) -- it is never used to admit stock or to feed any approval/money gate. No evaluate_gate/estimated_cost_cents/money-commit path exists in the inventory route or store at all, confirmed by both direct source reading and inventory.rs's own `inventory_routes_move_no_money` guard test (asserts the source contains no evaluate_gate/cogs_cents/journal_entry/money_commitment token). Original wave3-audit finding was accurate for the pre-refoundation flat crate; it does not map onto current code.
issues.evidence_ref: crates/cap/chronica-cap-erp-commerce-ops-routes/src/inventory.rs receive_stock (unitCostCents required, line ~299); crates/adapter/chronica-adapter-inventory-ledger/src/lib.rs record_receipt; crates/core/chronica-core-erp-inventory/src/lib.rs StockLedger::receive/issue (no zero-derived admission path)
issues.fix_ref: extinguished-by-refoundation (no P1 code change in DEBT.BATCH-1; adjustment_action path no longer exists, current receive path always requires an explicit unit_cost_cents)

issues.title: AVCO front-drain leaves stale per-layer costs
issues.detail: DEBT.BATCH-1 (2026-09) re-audit confirmed the defect survived refoundation into StockLedger::issue (chronica-core-erp-inventory/src/lib.rs): issue() under AVCO drained front layers at their ORIGINAL per-layer cost, leaving whatever historical layer cost happened to remain; the next avco_unit_cost_cents() call drifted from the true moving-average purely due to drain order (proved: 10@1000+10@2000 blended 1500, issue 10, remaining read as 2000). Initial fix (90bfb850) collapsed the remainder into ONE synthetic layer at (pre-issue valuation - cogs)/remaining_units, which architect review found could silently drop an indivisible integer-cent remainder (e.g. 2@100+1@101=301, issue 1: true remaining valuation is 201, not evenly divisible by 2 units). DEBT.BATCH-1R closes that gap: the remaining AVCO state is normalized into an exact quotient/remainder synthetic representation using AT MOST TWO integer-cent layers (quotient_remainder_layers), preserving the exact post-COGS valuation while still preventing historical receipt-layer costs from becoming the new AVCO rate. No fractional-cent precision added; FIFO/LIFO unchanged.

issues.title: JAdES report collapses INDETERMINATE into failure (over-claims)
issues.detail: report.rs reports a parse-failed/unresolvable-DID check byte-identically to a genuine failure; DSS returns INDETERMINATE. Fix: tri-state CheckState{Held,Failed,Indeterminate}; map UnresolvableDid/MalformedJws->Indeterminate. Mirrors RevocationState honesty rule.

issues.title: JAdES-B report unlabeled, mistakable for T/LT/LTA
issues.detail: report carries no timestamp/revocation requirement + no conformance-level stamp. Fix: stamp JAdES-B + mark timestamp/revocation NotChecked.

issues.title: Caption paginates on silence-gap not page-duration
issues.detail: caption_layout.rs paginate splits on inter-token silence gap; remotion splits on accumulated page duration. Continuous speech = one giant page. Fix: split on tok.end_ms-current_start>combine_within_ms.

issues.title: Spring advance missing remotion 64ms dt clamp
issues.detail: transition_timing.rs advance omits dt=min(now-last,64ms); at fps<16 trajectories diverge hard. Fix: dt=(1.0/fps).min(0.064).

issues.title: Workflow subgraph drops nodes on diamond graphs
issues.detail: graph.rs subgraph_recursive keeps first branch reaching trigger, not union of all reaching branches; multi-path graphs lose interior nodes. Fix: union every reaching branch + diamond test.

issues.title: Ambiguous +1/+7 dialing codes resolve to one ISO
issues.detail: country_codes.rs +1 (US/CA/Caribbean), +7 (RU/KZ) collapse to one primary; caller only sees ambiguous=true. Fix: model ambiguous codes as an ISO member set.

issues.title: Correlation confidence uses noisy-OR (amplifies AND-rules)
issues.detail: chronica-commerce-signals combine_confidence (correlation.rs:52-53, listing_drift.rs:42-49) uses noisy-OR for conjunctive AND-rules, so a 2-condition rule's derived confidence EXCEEDS every input (0.6&0.7->0.88) instead of decaying to the weakest link. Inflates advisory certainty fed to simulation. Fix: min (or product) for conjunctive rules; reserve noisy-OR for corroborating same-claim evidence.

issues.title: DistributionSummary percentiles are nearest-rank (P50 != median on even n)
issues.detail: chronica-simulation distribution.rs:104 percentile uses .round() nearest-rank, so P50 is not the true median on even-length samples and P10/P90 snap to a single sample. Money-safe (gate/EV untouched, verified). Fix: document nearest-rank convention or switch to linear interpolation.

issues.title: Clip owner can clip another user's private note (visibility-blind)
issues.detail: chronica-social add_note_to_clip (clip_store.rs:314) validates the note only via company-scoped note_store::get_note which ignores NoteVisibility, so any clip owner can clip another user's private/followers/DM note. Not live (readers #[ignore] db tests). Fix: filter get_note by visibility/author so non-public notes of others are not clippable.

issues.title: list_clip_notes/favorite_clip not owner/public-gated (private clip leak)
issues.detail: chronica-social list_clip_notes (clip_store.rs:378) and favorite_clip (408) are only company-scoped, not owner-or-public gated, so any company user can enumerate a private clip's timeline or favorite a private clip they don't own. Fix: require caller==owner OR clip.is_public in the existence check.

issues.title: Migration 0099 clips: no FK/ON DELETE (orphans on future delete_clip)
issues.detail: 0099_social_clips.sql: social_clip_notes.clip_id + social_clip_favorites.clip_id have no FK to social_clips and no ON DELETE, so a future delete_clip orphans all membership+favorite rows. Fix: add FK ... REFERENCES social_clips(id) ON DELETE CASCADE before shipping delete_clip.

issues.title: clip_store.rs 785 lines (god-file) + N+1 note fetch
issues.detail: chronica-social clip_store.rs ~785 lines exceeds 500 split-smell; split by cohesion (clip_row/crud/membership/favorite). Also list_clip_notes does N+1 get_note; use WHERE id = ANY($ids) AND company_id=$c preserving order.

issues.title: Relocate attribute-similarity is exact-Jaccard, not Scrapling fuzzy ratio
issues.detail: chronica-browser relocate.rs:43-70 scores attributes with set-Jaccard over exact key=value pairs; Scrapling __are_alike averages per-attribute SequenceMatcher.ratio() over len(candidate_attributes). class=btn->btn-primary scores ~0.6 in donor but 0.0 here, so real near-misses (the whole point of self-healing relocation) are dropped; the 0.2 threshold also means something different. Fix: per-key string-ratio averaged over candidate-attr count.

issues.title: ElementFingerprint lacks path_signature -> distinct nodes collide
issues.detail: chronica-browser fingerprint.rs: ElementFingerprint holds only attribute_hash, so two structurally-different nodes with identical attributes produce EQUAL fingerprints; fingerprint()-alone identity collides. Also the _get_hash fidelity claim is inaccurate (Scrapling _get_hash hashes the selector identifier string, not attributes). Fix: fold path_signature into the struct/hash; correct the doc.

issues.title: find_similar doesn't exclude the target (matches itself)
issues.detail: chronica-browser relocate.rs:86 find_similar never excludes the target node; Scrapling skips it (potential_match != root). In the natural re-snapshot-whole-DOM flow the target matches itself and is returned as its own relocation; also no deterministic tiebreak and the score is discarded so callers can't rank. Fix: filter out node==target; return (&DomNode,f32) pairs.

issues.title: Marketplace-health derived confidence not clamped to [0,1]
issues.detail: chronica-marketplaces environment_health.rs + competitiveness.rs average raw SignalCommon.confidence without clamping to [0,1], so a malformed >1.0 input yields derived confidence >1.0; the sibling commerce-signals combine_confidence clamps first. Advisory-only (can't gate money). Fix: clamp each contributing confidence to 0.0..=1.0 before the mean.

issues.title: fee_confidences includes non-contributing (delta=None) signals
issues.detail: chronica-marketplaces environment_health.rs:104: fee_confidences collected from ALL fee_signals, but fee_drift only uses delta()=Some signals; a previous_value=None signal inflates confidence without contributing to the trend. Fix: derive fee_confidences only from signals whose delta() is Some.

issues.title: Selector accname omits wrapping-label parent_text for text inputs
issues.detail: chronica-browser aria.rs:494: accessible-name for a label-wrapped text input never consults parent_text (ALWAYS_ALLOWS_NAME_FROM_CONTENT excludes textbox); Playwright roleUtils step 2e returns the associated-label text for INPUT/TEXTAREA/SELECT. Selector unaffected (a separate Label candidate is still emitted); only the computed accname string is understated. Fix: for INPUT/TEXTAREA/SELECT with parent_tag==label and no aria-label/placeholder, fall back to parent_text.

issues.title: Selector-gen omits [name=]/[type=] candidates for form controls
issues.detail: chronica-browser selector_gen.rs:238-305 omits Playwright's kCSSInputTypeNameScore [name=...]/[type=...] candidates for BUTTON/FORM/INPUT/SELECT/TEXTAREA/OUTPUT, so a control identified only by name/type falls to the CSS positional fallback (less stable). Fix: add a [name=]/tag[type=] candidate at CSS_INPUT_TYPE_NAME_SCORE for the donor node-name set.

issues.title: record_note_hashtags never called by create_note (feature inert)
issues.detail: chronica-social hashtag_store.rs:169 record_note_hashtags (the extract-on-note-create hook) has NO caller — create_note never invokes it, so no hashtag is recorded in production; the feature is dead code until wired. Same last-mile gap as [[dispatch-name-the-deliverable-crate]] (wave-104 VC store). Fix: call record_note_hashtags from the create_note path (same tx, passing note tags/author/created_at).

issues.title: trending() LIMIT truncates bucket rows alphabetically, not distinct tags
issues.detail: hashtag_store.rs:226: trending() applies LIMIT 2000 to raw (name,bucket) JOIN rows ordered by name ASC, truncating BUCKET rows alphabetically — drops later-alphabet tags AND undercounts a surviving tag whose buckets straddle the cutoff. Fix: aggregate/limit by DISTINCT tag (GROUP BY hashtag_id capped to N tags).

issues.title: record_hashtag_use 4 statements without a transaction (count drift)
issues.detail: hashtag_store.rs:104-167 fires 4 awaited statements (upsert tag, insert author, conditional mention bump, bucket upsert) with no surrounding tx; a mid-sequence failure leaves attached_count incremented but author/bucket rows absent -> permanent drift. Fix: wrap per-tag writes in one pg.pool().begin() tx.

issues.title: Hashtag counts never decrement on note delete/edit (drift up)
issues.detail: hashtag_store.rs has no decrement path; note delete/edit never rolls back attached/mentioned/bucket counts, so trend/reach drift upward forever. Fix: add record_note_hashtags_removed (guard mentioned_count against the author's other notes still using the tag) or document delete out-of-scope.

issues.title: List timeline folds members' PRIVATE notes (no visibility filter)
issues.detail: chronica-social user_list_store.rs:319-350 list_user_list_notes folds author_user_did=ANY(members) with NO visibility predicate, so a listed member's Followers/Specified/Home (private/DM) notes leak into any caller's list timeline. Not live (readers #[ignore] db tests). Fix: add a visibility clause (first cut visibility='public') matching note_store's timeline. Part of the social-visibility permission slice (with clips-private-note-clippable).

issues.title: List timeline/roster not owner-or-public gated (private list leak)
issues.detail: chronica-social list_user_list_notes + list_members (user_list_store.rs:294-350) are tenant-scoped only, not owner-or-public gated, so any same-company caller who names a list_id reads a private list's member roster + members' notes. is_public exists but is never enforced. Fix: gate on caller==owner OR is_public before resolving. Groups with clips-readers-not-owner-gated.

issues.title: user_list_store.rs 622 lines (god-file) + note-projection dup + migration no-FK
issues.detail: chronica-social user_list_store.rs ~622 lines mixes rows/mappers/timeline/8 fns/tests; split into user_list_store/{lists,members,timeline,rows}.rs. Also duplicates note_store json_strvec/NoteRow::map/NOTE_COLS (drift risk — expose pub(crate) + reuse). Migration 0101 has no FK/ON DELETE on member.user_list_id + no delete_user_list. Fix: split + reuse note projection + add delete_user_list/cascade.

issues.title: erp_reports: cross-company 403 (tenancy) untested at router level
issues.detail: chronica-api erp_reports.rs: all 12 tests call handlers directly, bypassing require_company_scope, so the cross-company 403 denial the lane relies on for tenancy is untested here. vault SecretSensitivity is caller-supplied with no ref-path backstop — mis-classifying a CrownJewel ref as Normal silently bypasses the board (fail-open classification)
issues.detail: proxy.rs:96 execute() takes sensitivity from the caller; quorum.rs:64 Normal=>Ok(()) never consults the board; crate deliberately never infers from the ref path (quorum.rs:27). No ref->sensitivity registry; CredentialRef/CapabilityScopedLease carry no sensitivity field. Fix at the wiring layer BEFORE live: derive sensitivity from a trusted server-side registry keyed on ref path (fail-closed default CrownJewel for bank/pki patterns), bind into the lease at issuance so it travels with the capability. Money-adjacent design decision — Brain-owned. MITIGATED after wave-6 FINAL-93EA remediation (issue #550): execute()'s first real prod call site (chronica-api::routes::companies::vault_secret_verify) always calls CredentialInjectionProxy::with_policy(...) with a configured crown-jewel path-pattern floor. FIXED at the crate-API-default level in the wave-6 Stage-1 review revision: CredentialInjectionProxy::new()'s default is now SensitivityPolicy::default_fail_closed() (banks/, payment/, pki/ patterns), not SensitivityPolicy::empty() — a future caller who does not configure an explicit policy still gets a real structural floor instead of zero. Residual risk (by design, not a defect): a caller can still explicitly pass SecretSensitivity::Normal for a credential path outside the baseline 3 patterns and it will not be escalated — a full fix requires the trusted server-side ref-path registry described above, which remains a separate, larger, Brain-owned design decision.

issues.title: vault proxy.backend() exposes pub VaultBackend::fetch — an ungated 2nd path to CrownJewel plaintext that skips execute()s quorum gate
issues.detail: proxy.rs:68 backend() returns &B; VaultBackend::fetch (backend.rs:20, re-exported lib.rs:50) needs only ref+lease (no sensitivity/quorum). Trace: backend().issue_lease() -> backend().fetch() -> Secret::expose() reads crown-jewel plaintext with no board approval. require_quorum_for_read is called only at proxy.rs:108. The tripwire test (proxy.rs:329) exercises only execute(), giving false crate-wide assurance. LATENT: no external consumers. Fix before live: narrow backend() to a health-only view / non-fetch trait, or move the quorum obligation into the backend; add a test asserting the direct-fetch path is gated/absent. FIXED wave-6 FINAL-93EA remediation (issue #550): `backend()` is now `#[cfg(test)]`-only — no production code (in this crate or any caller) can reach it; production callers drive the backend only through `execute()`.
issues.source: adversarial-verify wf_a12b985c-189 (api-surface-escape lens, the one confirmed bypass, HIGH)

issues.title: vault crown-jewel reads emit no VAULT-INV-3 SecretAccess access-audit WorkflowEvent (deferred) — no immutable audit trail on an authority surface
issues.detail: proxy.rs:24-26 documents the access-audit emission as deferred/absent; grep finds no SecretAccess{Requested,Granted,Denied} EventType. A gate-approved OR gate-denied crown-jewel read leaves no immutable record. LATENT (WCS Stage-5 sink WR-1-gated/unwired) but a missing obligation that MUST land before any live wiring. This is the 2nd half of the original vault-quorum finding, split out. FIXED wave-6 FINAL-93EA remediation (issue #550): the real production caller (`chronica-api::routes::companies::vault_secret_verify`) emits `chronica_events::BusinessEventKind::SecretAccess{Requested,Granted,Denied,Quarantined}` (added this wave) via the live `chronica_crm::store::business_event_store::capture_event` chokepoint for every terminal outcome — not the originally-planned `chronica-record-sync`/`WorkflowEngine::emit()` mechanism (that crate is itself a zero-caller island), but a real, live, tested audit trail.

issues.title: chronica-routines SecretResolver::resolve_by_name reads company_secrets plaintext with NO crown-jewel/quorum tier — a parallel secret path unaligned with the vault crown-jewel model
issues.detail: secret_resolver.rs:127-226 resolves company secrets to SecretMaterial plaintext directly from Postgres with tenant-ownership + audit but no board-approval/crown-jewel tier. Reads company_secrets rows (not vault:// refs) so not a strict vault bypass, but means read-a-money-capable-secret-plaintext is reachable with no quorum gate at all. The two secret subsystems are unaligned on the crown-jewel concept — reconcile the sensitivity model across both. FIXED: the ONE real call site, chronica-api::engine_boundary::DbBoundarySecretResolver::resolve_at_boundary, now classifies secret_ref.name with the same fail-closed chronica_vault::SensitivityPolicy every governed-vault HTTP route uses, and gates a crown-jewel-classified name behind chronica_vault::require_quorum_for_read + the existing governed_vault::ApprovalQuorumSource (reused verbatim) before the DB-authoritative resolver is ever called; an unclassifiable (control-byte/homoglyph/%) name fails the same uniform way. chronica-vault itself is untouched (caller-side only); LiveExternalWrite/LiveMoney remain unconstructable (this seam is still pre-arm, test-only-constructed). New tests: crates/chronica-api/tests/engine_boundary_db.rs (crown_jewel_secret_name_is_refused_without_board_approval_before_any_decrypt, crown_jewel_secret_name_is_granted_with_a_recorded_board_approval, normal_secret_name_bypasses_quorum_and_never_consults_the_board, crown_jewel_case_variant_secret_name_cannot_bypass_quorum, homoglyph_secret_name_is_rejected_and_quorum_cannot_be_bypassed).

issues.title: vault OpenBaoBackend::build_client panics inside vaultrs on an empty/malformed endpoint address instead of returning a VaultError (Stage-1 review Finding F1)
issues.detail: openbao.rs's build_client called vaultrs's VaultClientSettingsBuilder::address(base_url) directly with no validation; vaultrs panics (not errors) on an empty or malformed URL. CHRONICA_VAULT_ADDR="" sets the env var to Ok(""), not Err, so a naive .ok()-only skip check in the OLD live_openbao_round_trip test never fired, and the empty string reached vaultrs's panicking parser — reproduced by an independent Stage-1 reviewer twice. FIXED: added validate_base_url() (empty/whitespace-only/schemeless/scheme-with-no-host all refused with VaultError::Backend, called before vaultrs ever sees the string) plus 5 new unit tests proving every case fails closed without panicking.

issues.title: vault's live_openbao_round_trip PR-body claim ("1 passed, run against a deterministic mock server") was never actually true — #[ignore]d + OPENBAO_ADDR-gated, so it either panicked (empty addr) or trivially skipped (unset addr) in every reproducible run
issues.detail: The old test's ignore-skip branch used `let Ok(addr) = std::env::var("OPENBAO_ADDR") else { return }` — in CI/sandboxes where the var is genuinely unset this always trivially skips and never exercises a round trip; setting it to an empty string (as literally documented) instead panicked (see vault-openbao-empty-address-panics-not-fails-closed). FIXED: replaced with round_trip_actually_executes_against_a_deterministic_mock_server — NOT #[ignore]d, needs no env var, always runs a real connect->issue_lease->fetch round trip against the same in-process mock every other openbao.rs test uses, asserting the mock was hit exactly once. The old opt-in real-server smoke test is kept (renamed optional_live_external_server_smoke_test, still #[ignore]d) but is now clearly labeled optional and no longer the only claimed round-trip coverage.

issues.title: vault OpenBaoBackend::check_holding_scope fails OPEN (allows) when a reference declares a holdings/<id> scope but the connection has no configured namespace to verify it against
issues.detail: check_holding_scope only ever refused when BOTH the declared holding and the connected namespace were present and disagreed; a namespace-less backend handed a holdings-scoped ref was previously allowed through with nothing to check against. The crate's only production caller (vault_secret_verify.rs) always configures a namespace and never hits this branch, so this was latent, not exploited — correctly disclosed as an honest, deliberate gap by the prior revision. FIXED: a declared holding against a namespace-less connection now returns VaultError::CredentialHoldingMismatch (fail closed); a bare ref with no holdings/ prefix is unaffected (nothing to check either way). Test a_backend_with_no_configured_namespace_allows_any_holdings_prefixed_reference renamed/rewritten to a_backend_with_no_configured_namespace_refuses_a_holdings_prefixed_reference asserting the new refusal; a companion test proves a bare ref is still unaffected.

issues.title: vault_secret_verify.rs pre-backend validation refusals (malformed ref, blank taskId, bad sensitivity, missing config, tenant/holding denial) left no business_event row — only backend/lease/quorum-stage refusals were audited
issues.detail: Only Granted/Denied/Quarantined events fired, and only from the backend/lease/quorum stage onward; a caller sending a malformed request left zero durable trace, and SecretAccessRequested was defined but structurally unreachable (never emitted anywhere). FIXED: a SecretAccessRequested event is now emitted once, unconditionally, for every request past the shared assert_company_access tenant boundary (via record_requested, using the raw pre-validation request fields); a SecretAccessDenied event is now emitted for every refusal including the pre-backend ones, via a new deny_raw helper for the one refusal (malformed credentialRef) that has no parsed CredentialRef to audit against, and the existing deny helper reused for the rest (blank taskId, invalid sensitivity, tenant/holding denial, missing config, failed connect). Never leaks secret material (properties are always the caller's own reference-path/task-id/reason strings, never a resolved value). Idempotent under replay via the same capture_event (company_id, kind, occurredAt) dedup every other event in this route uses — 2 new dedicated replay tests (missing_vault_config_replay_is_idempotent, malformed_credential_ref_replay_is_idempotent) plus requested/denied-count assertions added to every existing refusal test (10 total pre-existing + new tests updated).
issues.source: stage1-review PR#586 comment 4950761461 (audit-evidence PARTIALLY CONFIRMED + 2 LOW findings)

issues.title: capability policy.secrets_encryption's target_module is "secrets" (plural) but chronica-vault's real module is named "secret" (singular) — stale in both the crate shard and the underlying capability row
issues.detail: crates/chronica-vault/.chronica/sub-cap-arch.jsonl's capability_architecture_link row inherits target_module from the canonical_capability row for policy.secrets_encryption (target_crate=chronica-vault), which reads target_module from docs/capabilities-cloud/cap-core.db's canonical_capability table (subdb:gen's actual data source in this environment; docs/capabilities.db itself is absent/local-only). REMAINS A SNAPSHOT-LEVEL FIX ONLY: docs/capabilities.db (the writable canonical DB) is absent from this checkout and was not corrected — a future real `caps:cloud-export` re-run by a local auditor with the true DB will silently regress this back to 'secrets' unless the same correction lands there too.

issues.title: vault_secret_verify.rs's VaultSecretVerifyRequest.sensitivity, when omitted from the request body, was silently treated as SecretSensitivity::Normal instead of rejected — a caller could skip declaring sensitivity entirely and get a quorum-free grant for a crown-jewel-shaped path
issues.detail: The sensitivity match's None arm defaulted to SecretSensitivity::Normal rather than refusing the request. An independent reviewer (PR#586 comment 4950917532) proved this with a real passing test: a request with no sensitivity field at all for an api-keys/provider-x-shaped credential ref was granted with no board approval consultation, even though the route's own default_crown_jewel_patterns() would have escalated an EXPLICIT crown_jewel declaration for a matching path. This was a caller-side (chronica-api) gap, not a chronica-vault crate gap: CredentialInjectionProxy::execute's sensitivity.max(self.sensitivity_policy.classify(credential_ref)) stricter-of-client-vs-server logic in proxy.rs was already correct and unaffected — the omission never reached that logic with a meaningful value to escalate. FIXED: the sensitivity match's None arm now calls deny() with a 422 "missing_sensitivity" reason ("sensitivity is required (\"normal\" or \"crown_jewel\") and is never defaulted") instead of defaulting. New tests: missing_sensitivity_is_rejected_422, missing_sensitivity_replay_is_idempotent (proves the 422 refusal is itself durably audited and idempotent under replay, consistent with every other pre-backend refusal in this route), sensitivity_downgrade_is_overridden_by_structural_policy (proves an explicit caller-declared "normal" for a server-classified crown-jewel path is still escalated, confirming the crate-side stricter-of-two-values logic this fix sits on top of remains correct).
issues.source: stage1-review PR#586 comment 4950917532 (MEDIUM finding 1: sensitivity omission defaults to Normal)

issues.title: vault_secret_verify.rs's Requested/Denied audit writes discarded capture_event's Result (`let _ = capture_event(...).await;`) — a durable-write failure after a real backend fetch/injection could leave zero durable evidence of the grant
issues.detail: record_requested and the deny()/deny_raw() refusal helpers called capture_event and threw away the Result, so a transient DB failure at exactly the wrong moment (mid-request, or on the terminal Granted write after a real secret had already been fetched and handed to the sink) would silently lose the audit row with no operator-visible signal — the caller would still receive a 200 with a real credential-verification outcome even though nothing durable proved the access happened. An independent reviewer (PR#586 comment 4950917532) proved the sink-injection-with-zero-durable-evidence path was reachable. FIXED: added require_durable_capture(), an exhaustive (no wildcard) match over every CaptureOutcome variant that either returns Ok(DurableCapture::{Created,Duplicate}) or Err(an operator-visible failure Response) — a caller of this function cannot ignore a failure outcome, since the Err(Response) must be propagated to type-check. Every audit write in the route (record_requested, deny, deny_raw, respond_granted) now goes through this helper. record_requested's call site gates immediately after the shared tenant-boundary check succeeds: `if let Err(failure) = record_requested(...).await { return failure; }` — Requested must durably commit BEFORE any further ref-parsing, backend connection, or sink access proceeds, closing the window where a real injection could occur with zero durable trail. respond_granted preserves its pre-existing Duplicate->409 CONFLICT semantics (distinct from record_requested/deny's "Duplicate is fine, proceed" treatment) via require_durable_capture's 3-way Ok(Created)/Ok(Duplicate)/Err(Response) return rather than collapsing Duplicate into unconditional success. New test: audit_store_write_failure_refuses_before_any_backend_or_sink_access — deterministically trips capture_event's own PropertiesTooLarge outcome via an oversized (80KB) taskId (below axum's 25MiB body-size limit, so it reaches the handler), and asserts HTTP 500, zero business_event rows of any kind, and no vault backend env configured at all — proving structurally, not just empirically, that backend/sink access was never attempted. Plus 8 new unit tests exhaustively covering require_durable_capture's match arms.
issues.source: stage1-review PR#586 comment 4950917532 (MEDIUM finding 2: discarded capture_event Result on the audit path)

issues.title: the opt-in optional_live_external_server_smoke_test still raised an opaque .unwrap() panic (not an informative failure) when OPENBAO_ADDR was set to a nonblank, malformed value
issues.detail: The test's connect_token(&addr, ...) call was followed by a raw .unwrap(), so a malformed nonblank OPENBAO_ADDR (e.g. missing scheme, unreachable host) produced Rust's generic 'called Result::unwrap() on an Err value' panic with no context naming the actual cause, making a CI/local failure harder to diagnose than necessary for an opt-in manual smoke test. Verified via OPENBAO_ADDR="not-a-valid-url" cargo test -p chronica-vault -- --include-ignored optional_live_external_server_smoke_test: the test still fails (correctly — it is not a live server), but the panic message now names the actual cause instead of an opaque unwrap.

issues.title: vault SensitivityPolicy::classify performed pure case-sensitive string matching with no canonicalization — a mixed-case or alias-shaped credential reference could dodge the crown-jewel quorum floor entirely
issues.detail: chronica-vault/src/sensitivity.rs's normalized_credential_path/pattern_matches compared a classified reference path against configured crown-jewel patterns (e.g. 'banks/') byte-for-byte, with no case-fold, no separator-collapse, and no rejection of percent-encoded ambiguity. An independent exact-head reviewer (PR#586 comment 4951160249) named this a hard admission blocker: a client (or an operator who stored a secret under a differently-cased path) could submit `vault://holdings/<id>/BANKS/mufg` and have it classified Normal instead of CrownJewel, silently bypassing board quorum for a bank-credential-shaped read. FIXED at the root, in two places: (1) chronica-vault/src/types.rs's CredentialRef::parse now rejects ANY segment containing a raw '%' fail-closed (percent-encoding is never decoded — an ambiguous reference is refused outright, closing the 'alias form' half of the finding); (2) chronica-vault/src/sensitivity.rs adds canonicalize_match_key (ASCII case-fold + collapse repeated '/' + trim), applied identically to BOTH the classified path (normalized_credential_path) and every configured pattern (normalize_policy_pattern) — so case/whitespace/separator variance on EITHER side can never desynchronize the comparison, while the segment-boundary check (a sibling prefix like 'pki/rooted' must not inherit the 'pki/root' floor) is preserved under the fold. The RAW, case-preserving reference is still what OpenBao's own KV storage (openbao.rs's kv_path, separately) and the audit trail use — canonicalization is a SAFETY-NET applied only at the classification layer, never changing which physical secret is fetched. 6 new adversarial crate-level tests (sensitivity.rs: case-variance-cannot-bypass, operator-pattern-case-is-also-normalized, case-fold-does-not-break-segment-boundary, doubled-separator-pattern-still-matches, canonicalize_match_key determinism/idempotency; types.rs: parse_rejects_percent_encoded_segments_fail_closed) plus 1 new end-to-end route-level adversarial test (vault_secret_verify_route.rs's crown_jewel_case_variant_credential_ref_cannot_bypass_quorum, zero mock-server responses queued, proving a mixed-case BANKS/Mufg ref still requires quorum via the real HTTP route, not just in isolation).
issues.source: exact-head-review PR#586 comment 4951160249 (hard admission blocker 1: mixed-case/path-alias classification bypass, unclosed)

issues.title: vault_secret_verify.rs drove a real backend fetch + sink injection directly, with only a best-effort terminal capture_event write recording the outcome — a crash or DB outage between injection and that write left ZERO durable evidence of what actually happened, and a byte-identical retry re-ran the real fetch/inject/lease-issuance/quorum-consultation a second time
issues.detail: The prior (Stage-1 addendum) revision closed 'durable evidence BEFORE any backend/sink access' (a SecretAccessRequested row always commits first) but left the AFTER side open: by the time respond_granted's own capture_event call ran, CredentialInjectionProxy::execute had ALREADY fetched the secret and injected it into the sink; if that terminal capture_event write then failed, the only durable business_event row was the earlier Requested one — nothing durably recorded completed/granted/summary. Separately, an idempotent replay (the same occurredAt) deduped the AUDIT ROW via capture_event's own unique index but did NOT deduplicate the underlying vault OPERATION — a replay re-ran a full fetch+inject+lease-issuance+quorum-consultation, which the reviewer traced directly in the code and confirmed by needing 2 queued mock responses for a single replay test. An independent exact-head reviewer (PR#586 comment 4951160249) named both halves of this a hard admission blocker: 'durable completed-or-failed outcome afterward: NOT CLOSED' and 'no replay may re-fetch/re-inject'. FIXED with a real durable idempotent attempt state machine/outbox (migration 0153, chronica-api's new vault_secret_access_attempt module — chronica-vault itself stays approvals/state-machine-free, VAULT-INV-5): claim_attempt durably commits a 'pending' row BEFORE connect_token/issue_lease/execute are ever reached, keyed on (company_id, idempotency_key) where idempotency_key is the caller's occurredAt when supplied (reusing the SAME replay identity business_event's own dedup uses) or a DB-minted gen_random_uuid() otherwise (preserving the pre-existing 'no occurredAt means no dedup' contract exactly). A Fresh claim proceeds to the real backend/sink access; mark_completed (called BEFORE respond_granted's own separate capture_event write, so it durably records completed/outcome/summary independent of whether that write also succeeds) or mark_failed finalizes it via a WHERE status='pending' compare-and-swap, so a row can be finalized AT MOST ONCE. A Terminal claim (a prior attempt already completed or failed) replays the SAME response WITHOUT touching the backend/sink again — respond_granted's own capture_event Duplicate-dedup still produces the exact same 409 a replayed grant has always returned, now with zero re-fetch underneath it. A ReconciledFailed claim (a prior attempt found STILL pending — a worker crash or a terminal-write DB outage) atomically reconciles the stuck row to failed via the SAME compare-and-swap and returns a definitive failure, NEVER re-attempting the backend/sink (since it is structurally unknown whether the original attempt already ran fetch/inject). 9 new failure-injection tests prove all 5 reviewer-named crash scenarios with real code, not just unit coverage in isolation: crash before fetch (route-level, a manually-seeded stuck-pending row is reconciled with zero mock-server responses queued), backend failure + replay-does-not-refetch (route-level, exactly ONE mock response queued, the replay reconstructs the identical failure), sink failure (chronica-vault crate-level, a MockSink that always errors proves execute() surfaces Err — never a false Ok(()) — after a genuine single fetch, closing the gap between 'backend failure' and 'sink failure' as DISTINCT scenarios), terminal-write-outage + retry recovery (route-level, the completed row is forced back to pending simulating a lost terminal write, then reconciled to failed on retry with zero further mock responses), plus a dedicated granted-replay-never-refetches route-level test (only ONE mock response ever queued for a replayed grant) and 5 repo-module-level tests (fresh-then-replay-is-terminal, mark_completed-then-replay, mark_failed-then-replay reconstructing the exact status/reason/detail, double-finalize-loses-the-CAS, no-idempotency-key-means-always-fresh).
issues.source: exact-head-review PR#586 comment 4951160249 (hard admission blocker 2: no durable completed-or-failed outcome afterward, replay re-fetches/re-injects, unclosed)

issues.title: CredentialRef::parse accepted non-ASCII/control/confusable path content and canonicalize_match_key was ASCII-only — a visually crown-jewel-shaped path (Cyrillic а, Greek α, fullwidth chars) could classify Normal, silently bypassing quorum
issues.detail: sensitivity.rs's canonicalize_match_key only case-folds and collapses ASCII separators; it never rejects or normalizes non-ASCII code points. A reference such as vault://holdings/<id>/bаnks/mufg (Cyrillic а, U+0430, visually identical to Latin 'a') would pass CredentialRef::parse unchanged and then fail to match the ASCII 'banks/' pattern under canonicalization, classifying Normal instead of CrownJewel — a homoglyph downgrade of the quorum floor. A second exact-head reviewer (PR#586 comment 4951364082) named this a residual: 'reject unsupported non-ASCII/control/confusable path content... do not silently transliterate or normalize one side differently.' FIXED at the trust boundary, fail-closed, with ONE shared grammar function used identically on both sides (no transliteration, no per-side normalization divergence): chronica-vault/src/types.rs adds is_ascii_path_safe (rejects any non-ASCII or ASCII-control byte), applied in CredentialRef::parse so a reference containing Cyrillic/Greek/fullwidth/combining/zero-width/control characters is refused outright (returns None, never constructed) — zero backend access, zero classification attempt possible. The SAME is_ascii_path_safe function is applied in sensitivity.rs's SensitivityPolicy::new so an operator-configured crown-jewel pattern containing non-ASCII/control content is also rejected at policy-construction time (dropped silently, same treatment as an empty pattern, never silently trusted) rather than being validated under a different grammar than the classified path. A related adjacent gap found via adversarial testing of this fix (not separately named by the reviewer but in the same fail-closed code path): a raw ASCII control byte (e.g. a trailing NUL) reaching vault_secret_verify.rs's pre-parse audit properties JSON crashed the durable Requested/Denied audit write with a 500 instead of returning the correct 422 (Postgres text/jsonb cannot store a literal NUL even JSON-escaped) — fixed with a new sanitize_for_audit() helper (replaces ASCII control bytes with U+FFFD before constructing the audit JSON, in both record_requested and deny_raw) so the audit trail itself can never be defeated by the same class of input, closing the loop on 'zero backend responses are consumed and quorum cannot be bypassed' end-to-end.
issues.source: exact-head-review PR#586 comment 4951364082 (residual 1: Unicode homoglyph downgrade, unclosed)

issues.title: a second concurrent identical request could reconcile an actively-owned, still-in-flight pending attempt straight to failed while the first request was still fetching/injecting — a false permanent failure record with no owner/lease concept
issues.detail: The prior revision's claim_attempt treated ANY pre-existing pending row found on conflict as a candidate for immediate fail-closed reconciliation (ReconciledFailed), with no notion of whether that row was still actively owned by an in-flight request or genuinely abandoned (crashed worker, dead connection). Under real concurrency, two near-simultaneous identical requests (same idempotency key) racing the same INSERT ... ON CONFLICT would let request B observe request A's row as merely 'pending' and reconcile it to failed — while request A was still mid-fetch/mid-inject — producing a false permanent failure record and a duplicate response that did not match what actually happened. A second exact-head reviewer (PR#586 comment 4951364082) named this a residual: 'a second request must not reconcile an actively-owned pending attempt to failed while the first request is still fetching/injecting... introduce durable ownership/lease semantics... only expired abandoned attempts reconcile fail-closed; only the owning token can CAS completed/failed.' FIXED with durable ownership/lease semantics added to migration 0153 (owner_token text NOT NULL, server-minted gen_random_uuid()::text at claim time; claimed_at timestamptz DEFAULT now(), a lease clock) and a new AttemptClaim::ActiveDuplicate variant: on conflict, claim_attempt now computes lease_active via a DB-side EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - claimed_at)) < ATTEMPT_LEASE_SECS (30s) comparison (DB-side to avoid app-clock skew) — if the existing row is still pending AND within its lease, the claimant returns ActiveDuplicate, a PURE READ that returns a stable in-progress/replay response (409, ACTIVE_DUPLICATE_DETAIL) WITHOUT any backend/sink access and WITHOUT mutating the owner's row. Only a pending row whose lease has EXPIRED (owner presumed crashed/abandoned) is reconciled to failed via the existing compare-and-swap. mark_completed and mark_failed are now owner-scoped CAS (WHERE id=$1 AND owner_token=$2 AND status='pending') so only the token that originally won the claim can ever finalize the row — a reconciler that raced past an expired lease cannot un-finalize a row the original owner is still in the middle of completing, and vice versa. 5 new tests prove this with real concurrency, not just seeded-row simulation: active_duplicate_is_read_only_and_never_reconciles_the_owners_row, concurrent_active_duplicate_never_causes_the_owner_to_lose_the_completion_cas, expired_lease_reconciles_to_failed_never_touching_a_still_active_one, finalize_with_the_wrong_owner_token_never_succeeds, and a route-level true_concurrent_duplicate_requests_one_fetch_one_injection_no_false_negative test that spawns two REAL concurrent HTTP requests (tokio::spawn racing against a delayed mock OpenBao) and asserts exactly one fetch, one injection, one completed row, one Granted event, zero Denied events, and a deterministic 409 for the loser — verified stable across 5 consecutive runs (not flaky).
issues.source: exact-head-review PR#586 comment 4951364082 (residual 2: concurrent duplicate false-negative, unclosed)
